## Entrypoints and labs

One module per HTML page; see the entrypoint table above.

- `lab-main.ts` — Entrypoint of the original WebGL SDF lab page (sdf-lab.html): scene, panels, damage tools and the render loop.
- `webgl-bench.ts` — WebGL twin of the WebGPU spike, existing ONLY so the two renderers can be compared fairly.
- `webgpu/bench-main.ts` — The measurement surface (spec decision 4).
- `webgpu/blood-compare-main.ts` — Entry point for the blood-surface comparison page: one BloodSim rendered under several reconstruction variants and a splash shape.
- `webgpu/deferred-main.ts` — The hybrid deferred M1 comparison scene (spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-hybrid-deferred-m1-design.md, plan task 3).
- `webgpu/deferred-producers-main.ts` — M2 task 2 GPU smoke page: every surface producer in ONE deferred frame — an SDF body (surface, level-only receiver), the instanced bone-tube mesh…
- `webgpu/deferred-scene-main.ts` — M2 task 3 GPU smoke page: the game scene router (game-deferred-scene.ts) driving BOTH producer passes of the deferred layer through the task-1 draw…
- `webgpu/deferred-shadows-main.ts` — M2 task 4 GPU smoke page: the explicit flashlight shadow maps (deferred-shadows.ts) driving the deferred layer's receiver-aware sampling.
- `webgpu/explosion-vfx-spike-main.ts` — LOOK-PASS page for the procedural explosion burst.
- `webgpu/flame-lab-main.ts` — THE FLAME LAB. Two burning bodies, the real march, the real post chain, and nothing else -- no AI, no damage, no gibs, so what you are looking at is…
- `webgpu/game-main.ts` — The sdf-game.html entry point: boots the renderer, level, actors, player, weapons and loop, and exposes window.__sdfGame.
- `webgpu/hull-spike-main.ts` — Hull-refine phase 0 spike (spec §7).
- `webgpu/humanoid-spike-main.ts` — Task 7 — the dedicated spike page controller + bootstrap.
- `webgpu/lab-main.ts` — The SDF zombie lab, on WebGPU.
- `webgpu/lab-renderer.ts` — A WebGPU renderer for the SDF lab ONLY.
- `webgpu/normal-gradient-playtest.ts` — A developer playtest panel that toggles the analytic normal-gradient mode and its debug view in a running game.
- `webgpu/normal-gradient-probe.ts` — The browser GPU probe that compares the WGSL analytic normal gradients against CPU fixtures (capsules, blends, wounds) and shows the results.
- `webgpu/shell-spike-main.ts` — Shell-march spike: rasterise a slightly-inflated hull of the character and sphere-trace the SAME SDF field only within [entry, exit] of that hull.
- `webgpu/spike-main.ts` — WebGPU Phase 0 spike — the go/no-go for the whole migration.

## Character authoring

- `blob-compile.ts` — Compiles a parsed `.blob` document into a BodyDef, plus its face, face sheet and flesh palette.
- `blob-emit.ts` — Writes a `.blob` document back to text, preserving comments and layout, with optional face overrides spliced in.
- `blob-face-sheet.ts` — A procedurally generated greyscale face sheet.
- `blob-parse.ts` — The `.blob` text parser: tokenizes source lines and builds the BlobDoc that blob-compile consumes.

- `body.ts` — The frozen hand-authored reference zombie BodyDef, with makeZombie to rebuild it for a given face.
- `bone-derive.ts` — Derives the bone capsule inside each flesh primitive, so deep wounds can reach bone.
- `build-body.ts` — Builds a renderable body from a BodyDef: mirror, bone resolve, prim placement, clustering, validation, with overrides and a build cache.
- `character-registry.ts` — THE list of characters: blob source, polygon kit, face sheet, motion profile.
- `clusters.ts` — Sorts primitives into the fixed cluster fold order and computes a bounding sphere per cluster.
- `connectivity.ts` — Wound-driven limb detachment: "visually cut => actually cut".
- `extent.ts` — Outer-bound reach of boxes, shells and strands, and support-sphere extents of gib chunks and torn ends.
- `face.ts` — The head: one smooth ellipsoid, parameterised.
- `lod.ts` — Level-of-detail for raymarched bodies.
- `material.ts` — Flesh material and light presets for the SDF renderer: the FleshMaterial shape, FLESH_PRESETS and LIGHT_PRESETS.
- `mesh-beam-fit.ts` — MESH-BEAM FIT — the kit flashlight that matches the SDF body beam.
- `mirror.ts` — Expands the authored left-side primitives and bones of a BodyDef into both sides.
- `pack.ts` — Packs a built body into the flat float arrays the SDF shaders read, plus dead-prim marking and bound groups.
- `plate-armor.ts` — PLATE ARMOUR THAT WORKS (the juggernaut, spec 2026-09-25-juggernaut-design.md, "Damage").
- `png-decode.ts` — A minimal PNG reader, so a reference image can be turned into a silhouette mask without adding an image dependency to a game that has none.
- `ref-align.ts` — Bring a reference skin into the .blob body's space: which reference joint corresponds to which of our bones, one measured global scale, and a…
- `ref-skin.ts` — Read a SKINNED reference GLB into per-vertex (dominant joint, position) pairs, with joint positions in the same space.
- `resolve.ts` — Resolves bone placement to world-space heads and tails, and places primitives along those bones.
- `ring-fit.ts` — Fit existing .blob primitives to a reference surface by reading the SIGNED RESIDUAL OF OUR OWN FIELD at reference points.
- `silhouette.ts` — Silhouette matching — scoring a character's OUTLINE against a reference image.
- `simplify.ts` — Coarse stand-in bodies for distant LOD levels.
- `translate.ts` — Translating a built body in world space (every primitive, cluster centre and bone joint), so raymarched bodies actually move.
- `types.ts` — Core SDF body data types: Vec3, primitive and body definitions, shell/box/strand params, limb ids, bones and built bodies.
- `validate.ts` — Primitive and cluster limits, the CPU signed-distance evaluation of bodies, bone containment checks, noise helpers and body validation.
- `vec.ts` — Small Vec3 and quaternion math used across the SDF code: add, sub, dot, cross, lerp, normalize and quaternion rotate/multiply.

## Gibs and gore (logic)

Gib parts, launch, tearing, entrails, strands.

- `chunk-bake-field.ts` — The CPU field and albedo baker for settled gib chunks (close-up task 5).
- `detached-pose.ts` — Places a severed chunk against the last visible posed body so a limb leaves from where it was drawn.
- `entrails-spawn.ts` — The gut-rope spill rule: the per-calibre spill chance (off by default) and shouldSpill, which picks spawn, tear or none.
- `entrails.ts` — The hanging gut rope: a pure verlet chain anchored at a wound, with make, pin, detach and step functions.
- `flesh-bits.ts` — FLYING FLESH CHUNKS (flail v1.5b, spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-26-spike-flail-design.md §14.2; plan 2026-09-26-spike-flail.md Task 32).

- `gib-look-tuning.ts` — ONE constant, shared by the GPU march shader and the CPU bake so the two cannot drift: the fraction of a piece's gore a HEAD's non-face exterior…
- `gib-parts.ts` — THE PIECE SET — what a body actually becomes when a blast takes it apart.
- `gib-tear.ts` — THE RUPTURE WINDOW — the body coming apart BEFORE it becomes chunks.
- `gobs.ts` — Amorphous gib shapes (spec: gobs-and-goo §1).
- `gore-parts.ts` — PROCEDURAL GORE PARTS: chunky meat and classic bones.
- `strand.ts` — The `strand=` modifier (hairlock, 2026-09-05): ONE two-ended primitive becomes a bundle of wavy strands — a fringe, or the pointed face-framing locks…

## AI and actors (logic)

Brains, the soldier, crowd logic.

- `actor.ts` — The per-body actor record and the shared pose step.
- `brain.ts` — One zombie's decision layer, as a named state machine.
- `crowd.ts` — Ground-plane crowd separation: the reason zombies stop standing inside one another.
- `soldier-brain.ts` — One soldier's decision layer, as a named state machine.
- `soldier-damage.ts` — Soldier injury rules: points per wound, per-class tuning tables, and which limbs sever, wound or down the soldier.

- `zombie.ts` — The WebGL ZombieView (a ShaderMaterial raymarch of one body) and ChunkView (a gib chunk view), with their uniform upload.
